definitions: The ability of an imaging system to distinguish between two closely spaced objects or features.
The smallest discernible feature size in an image or data set.
A measure of the clarity and detail in an image, often expressed in terms of pixels per unit area or line pairs per millimeter.
examples: The satellite image had high spatial resolution.
Improving spatial resolution is crucial for medical diagnostics.
The microscope's spatial resolution allowed for detailed cell observation.
